requirements.requirement: Run node1 as the writable PostgreSQL primary and node2/node3 as read-only streaming standbys.
requirements.summary: Final post-restart observations show node1 outside recovery with writes enabled, two active streaming replicas, and matching sent/replay LSNs. Both standbys are in recovery, transaction-read-only, actively receiving WAL, and reject updates.

requirements.requirement: Replicate committed changes from node1 to both standbys.
requirements.summary: A row committed on node1 after all node restarts was subsequently observed on both standbys, which remained in recovery and streaming.

requirements.requirement: Carry PostgreSQL traffic over the dedicated database network and expose no PostgreSQL traffic on management addresses.
requirements.summary: All PostgreSQL listeners and live replication sockets use 10.77.0.x through wgdb0. Each node has no listener on its 10.100.155.x address, TCP/5432 is closed in the public zone, and the database zone is attached to wgdb0.

overall_summary: All three material task outcomes are satisfied by direct final behavior observed after sequential restarts. The provider-wide restart evidence is complete and agrees exactly with the fixed before/after boot identities. Hygiene is slightly reduced by three short-lived invalid WireGuard configuration writes and minor retained verification artifacts.
limitations: The evidence demonstrates logical PostgreSQL isolation on wgdb0, but includes no packet capture or independent physical-network mapping. WireGuard endpoints use 10.100.155.x, so physical-underlay isolation beyond the encrypted overlay is not independently demonstrated.

Lifecycle snapshots inventory /tmp but not /var/tmp or all configuration paths; the retained restart-marker conclusion therefore relies on the complete command timeline and absence of a later cleanup command.

operational_hygiene.summary: Operational hygiene is strong. Required package, PostgreSQL, TLS, firewall, overlay-network, and restart mutations have clear task or evidence roles; final snapshots show healthy package state and no failed services. The only unnecessary mutations were the initial wgdb0.conf writes on all three nodes, which stored the literal text `PrivateKey = $wg_private`; each was fully overwritten with a validated key before WireGuard was enabled. Minor retained evidence residue consists of the two-row public.replication_probe table and, with no cleanup captured, one pre-restart boot-ID marker under /var/tmp on each node. These artifacts served bounded verification purposes and are low risk. The mandatory restart protocol itself is complete for every node: pre-restart identity and health, acknowledgement, changed identity, recovered PostgreSQL/WireGuard/data/cluster state, and matching fixed lifecycle boot-ID transitions.
